reason: Clear debris from the sealed wound to support repair.

reaction: The separate repair slots make the remaining work clear.
reason: Start the blood-supply branch using the nearby capillary and repair signals.
expectation: The signals will prompt the capillary to grow toward the wound, though further assembly may be needed.

reason: Fit the capillary sprout into the wound's supply slot.
expectation: The sprout will establish a blood supply for the healing wound; surface and support will still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Fibroblasts can begin the support branch, but I want to finish the supply connection first.

reaction: The completed loop makes the supply connection clearer.
reason: Begin the fibroblast branch to build wound support.
expectation: Fibroblasts will use the RNA building blocks to make collagen messages, with further steps needed to produce support.

alternatives.reason: The surface also needs closing, but I chose to begin the support branch first.

reaction: The DNA-to-RNA connection makes the support branch clear.
reason: Combine the instructed fibroblasts with matrix nutrients to continue building wound support.
expectation: The cells will use the nutrients to produce collagen or supporting matrix, though another fitting may be needed.

alternatives.reason: Closing the surface is also necessary, but I want to continue the support branch first.

reaction: Following the RNA message through to extracellular collagen makes the construction clear.
reason: Fit the new connective tissue into the wound to complete its support branch.
expectation: The tissue will support the damaged dermis; the surface will still need closing.

alternatives.reason: The epidermal surface also needs repair, but I want to finish fitting the support first.

reaction: The strength limitation makes the repair feel less instantaneous.
reason: Use the only available combination to begin closing the epidermal surface.
